sections.title: Situational Choice Questions
sections.description: Choose what you would do in each situation

questions.title: Repeated Failure, Different Cause Each Time
questions.scenario: You've lost the same game level 5 times, and each time for a different reason. What do you do?

options.text: Keep trying the same way
Change one thing and try again
Watch a replay of the last try first
Take a break, then come back

questions.title: Forgotten Homework, No Time to Fix It
questions.scenario: You forgot your homework at school and there's no time to fix it before class. What's your first move?

options.text: Tell the teacher before class starts
Quietly hope it doesn't come up
Ask a friend to glance at theirs quickly
Plan what you'll say if asked

questions.title: Split Attention — Real Cost to Helping
questions.scenario: You're 80% done with your own puzzle when a friend, who is stuck, asks for help. Helping might mean losing your own progress. What do you do?

options.text: Finish your puzzle first, then help
Stop and help immediately
Give a quick tip without stopping
Ask them to wait just a minute

questions.title: Hard Level — Every Option Has a Real Cost
questions.scenario: A level is very hard. What do you choose?

options.text: Skip it (miss a story clue)
Keep retrying (no limit, but you're getting tired)
Use a hint (lose 5 points)
Watch someone else first (takes 2 minutes)

questions.title: Long Repetitive Task, Mistakes Increasing
questions.scenario: You're sorting 50 shells. By shell 30, you notice more mistakes because you're tired. What do you do?

options.text: Push through at the same speed
Slow down to be careful
Take a short break, then continue
Speed up to just finish

questions.title: Disagreement Under a Tight Deadline
questions.scenario: Your teammate wants the rocket blue, you want it red — and it must be finished in 5 minutes. What do you do?

options.text: Suggest a compromise (like stripes or half-and-half)
Let them have their way to save time
Insist on your choice since you started it
Suggest voting or flipping a coin

questions.title: Confusing Rules, Social Waiting-Pressure
questions.scenario: A new board game's rules feel confusing, and others are waiting to start. What do you do?

options.text: Ask them to wait while you re-read
Start playing and learn as you go
Ask someone to explain just the first move
Watch one full round before joining

questions.title: Separated at a Fair — After the First Step Fails
questions.scenario: You get separated from your class. You go to the meeting point, but no one's there yet. What do you do next?

options.text: Wait and watch for a while
Ask a known adult for help
Look around the area and search for them
Go back to the same place and wait again

questions.title: Friend Bends a Rule — Social Cost to Speaking Up
questions.scenario: Your friend skips a rule to win a board game faster. Saying something might make it awkward; not saying anything doesn't feel fair. What do you do?

options.text: Speak up and point it out
Let it go this time
Suggest replaying the turn fairly
Mention the rule casually without blaming

questions.title: Math Problem, Two Genuine Ways In
questions.scenario: A tricky problem could be solved by drawing a picture (slower, clearer) or trying numbers directly (faster, riskier). You must start within 10 seconds. Which do you do?

options.text: Draw a picture
Try numbers directly

questions.title: Distraction With a Real, Irreversible Cost
questions.scenario: You're doing homework and hear your favorite show start. If you stop now, you'll miss the first 5 minutes forever — reruns skip that part. What do you do?

options.text: Keep working
Watch, planning to return to homework after
Stop and don't return

questions.title: Unfinished Group Work, Tomorrow's Deadline
questions.scenario: Your group presents tomorrow and one part isn't done. It's evening and everyone's tired. What do you do?

options.text: Do a smaller, realistic version to finish tonight
Push to finish the whole thing anyway
Leave it and hope for time in the morning
Ask the teacher for an extension

questions.title: Mistake With a Visible Emotional Reaction
questions.scenario: You accidentally knock over your sibling's block tower right as they finish it. They look upset. What do you do first?

options.text: Apologize and check on them
Start fixing the tower immediately
Explain it was an accident
Walk away and come back later

questions.title: Losing Repeatedly, With a Subtle Improvement Trend
questions.scenario: You're new to a sport. You lose every round, but each time by a little less. Do you notice, and what do you do next?

options.text: I notice I'm improving — keep going!
I'm still losing — maybe try something else
I'm not sure if I'm getting better, but I'll keep trying
It doesn't matter, I want to quit

questions.title: Sudden Decision During a Long Wait
questions.scenario: You're waiting in a long line, bored. Staff announce the ride closes in 3 minutes — you might not make it if you stay, or you could leave now for a shorter ride nearby. What do you do?

options.text: Stay and hope to make it
Switch to the shorter ride now
Ask staff for more information first

questions.title: Bridge vs. Long Way — Genuine Uncertainty
questions.scenario: A fast path crosses a bridge that might be wobbly — you're not sure. A slow path goes safely around. Which do you pick, without knowing for certain if the bridge is actually unsafe?

options.text: Take the bridge (fast but uncertain)
Go around (slow but safe)

questions.title: Guaranteed Small Reward vs. Uncertain Big Reward
questions.scenario: An unlocked chest has 10 coins for sure. A locked chest has either 50 coins or nothing, decided by a coin flip. Which do you pick?

options.text: Guaranteed 10 coins
50-or-nothing gamble

questions.title: Solo vs. Team — Explicit Trade-off
questions.scenario: Go on a mission alone (all credit is yours, but no help if stuck) or with a crew (help is always there, but credit is shared). Which do you pick?

options.text: Solo — all credit, no help
Team — shared credit, always help

questions.title: Hint Under Uncertainty, With a Timer
questions.scenario: You're stuck, with a timer running. A hint costs 5 points but you're not sure it will actually help. Do you use it, wait longer without it, or give up on this one?

options.text: Use the hint
Wait it out
Give up

questions.title: Fast-With-Mistakes vs. Slow-and-Careful
questions.scenario: In a maze, finishing fast might mean 2–3 wrong turns to undo; finishing slow means almost no wrong turns but takes much longer. There's no time limit today. Which do you pick?

options.text: Fast, expect some mistakes
Slow, aim for none

questions.title: Known-Okay Way vs. Unproven-Better Way
questions.scenario: You know a way to solve the puzzle that works but is slow. A friend says there's a faster way, but she hasn't tried it herself yet either. Which do you use?

options.text: Use the known way
Try the unproven new way
Ask friend to demonstrate first

questions.title: Finish Own Task vs. Help — Real Cost Attached
questions.scenario: You're almost done with your task. A friend is stuck and asks for help — but stopping means losing your progress and restarting later. Do you finish first, or help first?

options.text: Finish first
Help first

questions.title: Quick-Safe Guess vs. Slower Bigger-Reward Think
questions.scenario: A riddle: answer in 5 seconds for a small reward either way, or think for 30 seconds for a bigger reward, only if correct. Which do you choose?

options.text: Quick, safe — small reward guaranteed
Slower — bigger reward if right
